title: 43 Relationship between reproductive parameters and residual feed intake in yearling beef bulls
content:
Abstract
Residual feed intake (RFI) is a metric utilized to estimate feed efficiency, in which differences between actual and expected feed intake are assessed. Improving feed efficiency while ensuring optimal reproductive performance is essential for maximizing the profitability of beef industry. However, published data exhibit conflicting results concerning the negative effect of RFI on reproductive parameters. Therefore, our objective was to establish a comprehensive relationship between RFI and reproductive parameters in yearling bulls. Sixty, 10–12-month-old Brangus bulls were tested for feed efficiency over 56 d and ranked as feed efficient (LRFI) or inefficient (HRFI). Scrotal circumference (SC) was measured, blood samples were taken for testosterone concentration analysis, and semen samples were collected by electroejaculation at the beginning and at the end of the test. Fresh semen was visually evaluated for motility, morphology, and plasma membrane integrity (Table 1). Sperm kinematics and concentration were determined simultaneously via computer-assisted sperm analysis (CASA-IVOS II System) within 4 hr of collection in a medium designed for holding sperm (Table 2). Statistical analysis included repeated measures to assess interactions between group (LRFI, HRFI) and time (0 and 56 d of RFI measurement). The main effect of group did not affect CASA derived traits, while major (P < 0.04) and total defects (P = 0.01) were affected among visually evaluated traits. A time effect was observed in SC (P < 0.01) and testosterone concentration (P = 0.03), as well as in the amplitude of head displacement (P < 0.01), beat cross frequency (P < 0.01), linearity (P < 0.01) and curvilinear velocity (P < 0.01) among kinematic traits, while all visually evaluated traits were affected by time (P < 0.05) except for visual motility. An interaction effect (group x time) was observed in sperm linearity (P = 0.04) among kinematic traits, and plasma membrane integrity (P = 0.01) among visually evaluated traits. The results demonstrate that fertility-related measurements were independent of RFI in the evaluated bulls, with time emerging as the most significant determinant of the observed variability in the estimated parameters. These findings indicate that selecting young bulls based on RFI may not adversely impact semen quality parameters related to fertility.
